nodes.summary: For every hash function $h$ and every positive bucket count $m$, the finite map represented by the empty hash table with hash function $h$ and $m$ buckets is the empty finite map.
nodes.title: The empty hash table represents the empty map

nodes.summary: For every valid hash table $T$, every key $k$ and every value $v$, the finite map represented by the table obtained by inserting $k$ with value $v$ into $T$ equals the finite map represented by $T$ with $k$ bound to $v$, replacing any earlier binding of $k$.
nodes.title: Insertion commutes with the abstraction

nodes.summary: The finite map represented by a hash table with $m$ buckets is built from the list of all bindings of buckets $0, 1, \dots, m - 1$, concatenated in this order: it binds exactly the keys occurring in this list, and binds each such key to the value of its first binding in the list.
nodes.title: Finite map represented by a hash table

nodes.summary: For a hash function $h$ and a positive integer $m$, the empty hash table with hash function $h$ has $m$ buckets, each holding the empty chain.
nodes.title: Empty hash table

nodes.summary: For a key type $\alpha$, a value type $\beta$ and a hash function $h : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$, a hash table with hash function $h$ consists of a positive number $m$ of buckets and, for each bucket index $i < m$, a chain stored at bucket $i$: an association list of key–value pairs whose keys are pairwise distinct. The structure itself does not require keys to lie in their hash-selected bucket.
nodes.title: Hash table with separate chaining

nodes.summary: Inserting a key $k$ with value $v$ into a hash table with $m$ buckets and hash function $h$ keeps the bucket count and every bucket other than bucket $h(k) \bmod m$, and replaces the chain at bucket $h(k) \bmod m$ by that chain with $k$ bound to $v$: any earlier binding of $k$ in that chain is removed and the binding of $k$ to $v$ is added.
nodes.title: Insertion into a hash table

nodes.summary: For every valid hash table $T$ and every key $k$, looking up $k$ in the finite map represented by $T$ gives the same result as looking up $k$ in $T$.
nodes.title: Lookup agrees with the abstraction

nodes.summary: For every hash function $h$, every positive bucket count $m$ and every key $k$, looking up $k$ in the empty hash table with hash function $h$ and $m$ buckets finds no value.
nodes.title: Lookup in the empty hash table

nodes.summary: For every hash table $T$, all keys $k \ne k'$ and every value $v$, looking up $k'$ in the table obtained by inserting $k$ with value $v$ into $T$ gives the same result as looking up $k'$ in $T$, also when $k$ and $k'$ lie in the same bucket.
nodes.title: Insertion does not affect other keys

nodes.summary: For every hash table $T$, every key $k$ and every value $v$, looking up $k$ in the table obtained by inserting $k$ with value $v$ into $T$ returns $v$.
nodes.title: Hash table lookup after insertion

nodes.summary: For a hash table with hash function $h$ and $m$ buckets, looking up a key $k$ searches only the bucket with index $h(k) \bmod m$: the result is the value bound to $k$ in that bucket's association list, or nothing if $k$ has no binding there.
nodes.title: Hash table lookup

nodes.summary: For every hash function $h$ and every positive bucket count $m$, the empty hash table with hash function $h$ and $m$ buckets is valid.
nodes.title: The empty hash table is valid

nodes.summary: If a hash table is valid, then the table obtained from it by inserting a key $k$ with value $v$ (adding a new binding for $k$, or replacing the existing one) is again valid.
nodes.title: Insertion preserves validity of a hash table

nodes.summary: A hash table with hash function $h$ and $m$ buckets is valid when every binding lies in its hash-selected bucket: for every bucket index $i < m$ and every key $k$, if $k$ has a binding in bucket $i$, then $h(k) \bmod m = i$.
nodes.title: Valid hash table

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
